svg.title: See what your applications do
svg.desc: See what your applications do. Metrics per application: Requests, response times, errors, memory and CPU for every application, charted as they happen. A request inspector: The newest requests with status, timing, query string and headers. Cookies and authorization headers are never kept. Logs and terminals in a dock: Logs, Artisan, Tinker and a console at the bottom of the window. Artisan offers your models, tables and routes as you type. A database browser: Browse any table in one grid, and write SQL that completes tables and columns. MySQL, MariaDB and PostgreSQL. Draw your schema: For Laravel: tables and model relationships as blueprints. Drag one model onto another to relate them, and review the code first. Dependency audits: Audit Composer and JavaScript dependencies, and make package managers wait before installing brand-new releases. A command palette: Every page, application, Artisan command and action, a few keystrokes away. Two themes: Daybreak and Nightfall, or follow the system. Your choice reaches every window and the editor. An MCP server for AI agents: Turn it on and agents such as Claude Code can list sites, switch PHP, create databases and read caught mail. The phun command: Link, park, secure, share and switch PHP from your terminal. The app and the command share one daemon. Health checks with fixes: Built-in checks for DNS, certificates, ports and PHP, each with a one-click fix when something is off. Updates itself: Phun checks for new versions and installs them from the app, with the release notes beside them.
